gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-khojk: Existence draws curves and straights at exactly one width, like bent wire. Noto Serif Khojki is the softer partner, a text serif with short ascenders over big bowls and a faint swelling in each round letter.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-lao: Tube-like and industrial, with portholes for counters. Noto Serif Lao takes over below as a classic serif, its tall lowercase and gently shifting bowls softening what Existence holds rigid.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-makas: Noto Serif Makasar is a text serif with towering lowercase and a soft slide from heavy to light strokes. Existence, uniform in gauge, makes a stark partner above it.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-malay: Bookish and refined, Noto Serif Malayalam gives every small letter a big open counter, with bowls that thin gently. But Existence, smooth as plotter ink, stays industrial, so the classic serif below carries the reading with mild stress and solid strokes.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-np-hm: Existence has no hairlines at all, just stems matched to every other stroke, with terminals cut short. Noto Serif NP Hmong reads like a classic serif touched with charcoal, its lowercase rising near cap height for a literary, refined flow.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-old-u: Glassy portholes, industrial lines. Noto Serif Old Uyghur follows as a classic serif, its blown-bulb bowls and measured thick-thin difference like thread beside the yarn of Existence, a rolling-ball pen trail.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-oriya: Dignified and authoritative, Noto Serif Oriya is a classic serif with curves a touch heavier than its joins.
